title.quote: In-Context Learning for Text Classification with Many Labels
title.value: In-Context Learning for Text Classification with Many Labels

extractions.description: The paper applies retrieval-augmented in-context learning with frozen pre-trained dense retrievers (SBERT) and open-source LLMs (OPT, LLaMA, LLaMA-2) to text classification tasks with many labels (intent classification on BANKING77, HWU64, CLINC150 and fine-grained sentiment classification on GoEmotions), comparing against fine-tuned baselines (DeBERTa with Pfeiffer adapters, SetFit, ConvFit) and running ablations on label semantics, example similarity, and input-label correspondence.

type.quote: Testing with recent open-source LLMs (OPT, LLaMA), we set new state of the art performance in few-shot settings for three common intent classification datasets
type.justification: The paper runs experiments and reports empirical results.

name.quote: In-context learning (ICL) using large language models for tasks with many labels is challenging
name.justification: Core field advanced by the paper

name.quote: we use a pre-trained dense retrieval model to bypass this limitation
name.justification: The paper works on text classification with many labels

name.quote: we set new state of the art performance in few-shot settings for three common intent classification datasets
name.justification: Intent detection is a main application domain advanced

name.quote: We also surpass fine-tuned performance on fine-grained sentiment classification in certain cases.
name.justification: Sentiment classification is an evaluation domain

name.quote: By coupling the LLM with an external pre-trained dense retriever model
name.justification: Dense retrieval used as a component

name.quote: Models pre-trained on massive amounts of textual data
we use the SentenceTransformers library (Reimers and Gurevych, 2019a), and use the pre-trained “all-mpnet-base-v2” model (a 110M parameter model pre-trained on over 1 billion training pairs)
name.justification: The retrieval model used in all experiments
